chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Nahik from Ali ibn al-Harith from Sabbah al-Muzani from Najiya who said:

I saw a man in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I emancipated a female servant of mine, and I have been seeking to buy a servant for years but I cannot find one.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What does the servant do?' He said: 'She is a snake (hypocrite/unfamiliar).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Return her to her slavery. Whatever Allah has made one of you self-sufficient from emancipation, you are emancipating today, and it will be upon us tomorrow. It is not permissible for you to emancipate except one whom you recognize.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on emancipating a servant one does not know well?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises a man to retain his female servant, whom he describes as a 'snake' (implying hidden flaws or hypocrisy), rather than freeing her due to his inability to find a replacement. This illustrates the Shia juristic principle that emancipation (*itq*) is not merely a ritual act but requires the master's knowledge of the servant's character to ensure the act is beneficial and not detrimental to the household's stability. The Imam’s criterion of 'knowing' (*'arifa*) highlights the importance of discernment in social transactions, ensuring that freedom is granted to those who will uphold it responsibly.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from salma Bin Al Khattab, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Naheyk, from Ali Bin Al Haris, from Sabbah Al Muzny, from Najiya who said,

‘I saw a man in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I emancipated a female servant of mine and she was a sought after attendant for years. So what do I value upon her?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What does the attendant do?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She is a snake (hypocrite)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Return her in her slavery. Whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Made one of you to be self-sufficient from emancipation, you are emancipating today, and it would happen upon us<sup>asws</sup> tomorrow. It is not allowed for you that you emancipate except one whom you recognise’.
